newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: CONCERNS OVER THE IMPACT OF YOUTH DOLE CHANGES
The Howard Government's plans to scrap the dole for 16 and 17 year olds, has been met with the expected criticism from the Opposition and Democrats.
The Government is planning to replace the dole with a common youth allowance, aimed at encouraging teenagers to study longer.
A parental means tests on dole payments will also be imposed on unemployed aged 18 to 20.
Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley says planned changes amount to nothing more than an attempt to hide youth unemployment.
He says plans to cut out the allowance once a family income reaches $41,000 is unrealistic.
Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot says the youth allowance will be a great source of friction and family break-down.
GROUPS REJECT WIK PLAN WILL CUT COSTS
Aspects of the Prime Minister's 10 point Wik plan have attracted criticism from traditional land owners and land economists alike.
The Central Land Council has rejected claims the plan will dramatically cut the Northern Territory's native title bill.
Territory Treasurer Mike Reed claims the plan will save his Government a possible multi-Billion-dollar payout, by limiting compensation payments.
The Central Land Council says on the contrary, the plan will lead to protracted court cases, meaning costs will increase.
Meanwhile the Australian Institute of Land Valuers and Land Economists says the native title plan is flawed and agrees it will only lead to more, costly litigation.
HAWKE BACKS HOWARD'S STANCE ON HK HANDOVER
Former Labor Prime Minister, Bob Hawke, says he believes the Federal Government has made the right decision to attend the Hong Kong handover ceremony.
An international split has developed after the United States and Britain decided to boycott the swearing-in of Hong Kong's non-elected Legislature, when the colony reverts to Chinese rule.
Prime Minister John Howard has said that human rights concerns are best pursued through dialogue and he believes a boycott could harm Australia's interests.

Mr Hawke, who wept after the Tiannamen Square massacre in 1989, says Australia should not be leading the preaching brigade about a country which is making major progress towards the liberalisation of regimists.
GOVT TO WAIT AND SEE ON CONVENTION VOTE
The Parliamentary Secretary to the Prime Minister says he's not prepared to canvass what options are available if the Senate does not pass the government's Constitutional Convention legislation.
Senator Nick Minchin was commenting as the Senate is today set to consider amendments to the legislation for the planned Convention.
The Government wants a voluntary postal vote to elect delegates to the December Convention which will debate whether Australia should become a republic.
But the Opposition, Democrats and Greens Senators want a compulsory ballot to elect half of the 152 delegates.
Democrats leader Cherrl Kernot says the issue is so important that Australians should be required to turn up and legitimise the process.
OPPOSITION SUPPORTS HOWARD'S KLAN EXAMPLE
The Federal Opposition has endorsed the Prime Minister's plan to use a London address to liken Independent MP Pauline Hanson to U.S. Klu Klux Klan figure David Duke.
Mr Howard told a meeting of Coalition MP's before heading overseas the speech will highlight the fact that economic restructuring in a number of countries is turning out people with extreme views.
The Prime Minister plans to mention Ms Hanson along with Mr Duke and French National Front leader, Jean-Marie Le Pen.

Deputy Oposition Leader Gareth Evans says while it's a pity Mr Howard hasn't used this language before, he nonetheless believes the analogy is an apt way of countering Australia's image problem overseas.
NSW PREMIER TO FACE CENSURE MOTION
A NSW Independent MP says he intends moving a censure motion against Premier Bob Carr in parliament next week.
Peter MacDonald says his proposed motion, expected to be debated next Tuesday, includes censure of the Premier for what he claims is the government's repeated abuses of Lower House procedures.
Dr MacDonald claims Mr Carr has failed to uphold the letter and spirit of the Charter of Reform he signed with Lower House Independents in 1992.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
